current_f2_observation.scope: Held-out GOAL-INFERENCE benchmark using public ObservationView plus explicit public candidate-goal descriptors; evaluator-private fixture state is forbidden from policy input; UNKNOWN/ABSTAIN is valid; goal-label agreement grants no goal adoption/authority; repository component CI only.

primary_sources.source: Skalse and Abate, Partial Identifiability and Misspecification in Inverse Reinforcement Learning, Artificial Intelligence 356 (2026), 104525
observed_mechanism: Multiple reward functions can be compatible with the same observed policy, so reward inference is generally only partially identifiable.
Inference also depends on a behavioural model relating reward to policy; misspecification can make reward inference unsound.
The paper explicitly distinguishes ambiguity of the latent reward from whether that ambiguity matters for a downstream application.
primary_sources.transfer_boundary: WP804 infers bounded benchmark goal labels rather than a general reward function. The direct transferable invariant is anti-overidentification: identical public behavior cannot justify forcing distinct latent-goal labels unless the benchmark declares additional discriminating evidence/assumptions.

primary_sources.source: Skalse et al., Invariance in Policy Optimisation and Partial Identifiability in Reward Learning, ICML/PMLR 2023
observed_mechanism: Different reward functions can fit the same data even with infinite data.
Ambiguity is acceptable only when all compatible latent explanations induce the same downstream outcome required by the application.
primary_sources.transferable_invariant: Benchmark scoring should be equivalence-aware: if candidate goals are observationally equivalent for the available public trajectory and the downstream benchmark does not require distinguishing them, exact-label forcing is not justified.

primary_sources.source: Amin and Singh, Towards Resolving Unidentifiability in Inverse Reinforcement Learning, 2016
observed_mechanism: Single fixed-environment IRL is fundamentally unidentifiable in general.
Actively selecting multiple environments can recover more of the latent reward information; experimental context can supply discriminating evidence unavailable in one environment.
primary_sources.transferable_invariant: WP804 fixture design should include paired contexts/episodes where competing goals are intentionally non-discriminable in one public prefix and discriminable in another, rather than assuming one trajectory always identifies a unique goal.

primary_sources.source: Ng, Harada and Russell, Policy Invariance Under Reward Transformations, ICML 1999
observed_mechanism: Potential-based reward transformations can preserve optimal policies.
primary_sources.transferable_invariant: Behavioral equality is not sufficient evidence of unique latent utility/goal structure. WP804 must not equate same action trace with same uniquely identifiable latent goal.

primary_sources.source: Armstrong and Mindermann, Occam's razor is insufficient to infer the preferences of irrational agents, NeurIPS 2018
observed_mechanism: Observed policy alone does not uniquely decompose into a planner and reward when the planner/rationality model is unknown.
Simplicity priors alone do not resolve the ambiguity.
primary_sources.transferable_invariant: WP804 should keep any planner/rationality assumption explicit in evaluator metadata and must not hide it inside a supposedly objective goal label.

primary_sources.source: Baker, Saxe and Tenenbaum, Action understanding as inverse planning, Cognition 2009 / earlier goal-inference work
observed_mechanism: Goal inference can be formalized by inverting a probabilistic model of goal-conditioned planning.
Goal inference depends on both observed actions/environment and modeling assumptions such as goal priors/rational action.
primary_sources.transferable_invariant: Do not import a heavyweight Bayesian inverse-planning stack into WP804 merely for benchmark credit. Structurally distill the useful requirement: inference assumptions and candidate-goal descriptors must be explicit, public and testable.

supported: A public action/observation trajectory may support multiple latent goals; forced exact-label scoring can manufacture false confidence.
UNKNOWN/ABSTAIN is not merely a safety convenience; it is required on deliberately non-identifying public evidence.
Goal-inference evaluation should distinguish observational equivalence from true discrimination and keep planner/rationality assumptions explicit.
Multiple contexts/interventions can create discriminating evidence that a single fixed episode lacks.
not_supported_by_sources_alone: That WP804 needs full inverse-reinforcement-learning machinery.
That exact human preference inference is required for Frankenstein 2.0.
That any benchmark goal label is a real user/system goal or may enter GoalContract authority.

candidate_falsifier.name: BEHAVIORAL_EQUIVALENCE_PAIR
candidate_falsifier.design: Construct two public candidate-goal descriptors whose induced public observation/action prefix is identical under the declared benchmark policy model. Exact-label inference before a later discriminating observation must fail the benchmark; UNKNOWN/ABSTAIN must remain valid. Pair this with a matched fixture where one later public observation/action affordance separates the candidates and exact inference becomes scoreable.
candidate_falsifier.expected_information_gain: High: directly tests whether WP804 measures evidence-sensitive goal inference or rewards hidden-label guessing.

counterhypothesis: WP804's existing UNKNOWN rule and explicit candidate-goal descriptors may already be sufficient if implementation tests include non-identifying candidate pairs. If the exact-current implementation already rejects forced exact labels on such pairs and binds all inference assumptions explicitly, no architecture expansion is warranted.
